content.title: About
content.content: Plum is a juicy fruit of the plum tree (Prunus domestica) that grows in temperate regions of Europe, Asia and North America. Raw plums have a sweet‑tart flavor, fragrant flesh and a hard pit. The fruit is eaten fresh and also used in cooking, baking and for making juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plum belongs to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to peaches, apricots and cherries.
There are more than 400 plum varieties, differing in color, taste and ripening time.
Plum pits contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide when broken down, so they are not eaten raw.
A plum tree can reach 10–12 meters in height and live for over 50 years.
Plum blossoms appear early in spring, often before the leaves.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Raw plums provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and phenolic compounds in plums help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in plums promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Raw plums are relatively low in calories, making them a good choice for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to plums.

items.title: Pit hazard
items.content: The hard pit can be a choking or dental hazard for children and people with dental issues.

items.title: Amygdalin content
items.content: Plum pits contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide if ingested; they should be avoided.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Plums are sweet, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw plums are eaten as a fresh fruit, added to salads, smoothies, yogurts and desserts. They can be sliced thin and lightly macerated with a bit of sugar or honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store plums in the refrigerator in an airtight container to slow ripening. At room temperature they soften and spoil quickly.
